easy.def: A person who plans buildings.
examples: The architect drew a plan.
An architect designed the house.
The architect made a model.

more.def: A person whose job is to design buildings.
examples: The architect drew a plan for the new school.
An architect designed the museum.
The architect made a small model of the tower.

easy.def: A part of a place.
examples: The play area is big.
This area is quiet.
We ate in the picnic area.

more.def: A part of a place or space.
examples: The playground has an area for little kids.
Rain fell over a large area of the state.
Please stay in the picnic area.

easy.def: The size of a flat surface.
examples: We measured the area of the rug.
A big room has a large area.
The area of the field is huge.

more.def: The amount of flat space inside a shape, measured in squares.
examples: The area of a square that is three feet on each side is nine square feet.
Find the area of the garden before buying grass seed.
The area of the football field is huge.

easy.def: To say you do not agree, sometimes in a mad way.
examples: My brother and I argue about who goes first.
Do not argue with your sister.
They argue about which show to watch.

more.def: To disagree with someone in words, or to give reasons for what you think.
examples: The two friends began to argue about the rules of the game.
The players argued with the referee about the call.
She argued that recess should be ten minutes longer.

easy.def: An angry talk between people who do not agree.
examples: They had an argument.
The argument was about a toy.
I had an argument with my brother.

more.def: A disagreement in which people say angry things about what they think.
examples: The two brothers had an argument about the game.
We settled the argument by taking turns.
They had an argument over who got the last cookie.

easy.def: A reason you give to show something is true.
examples: Her argument was clear.
He gave a good argument.
I made an argument for more recess.

more.def: A set of reasons that you give to try to show that something is right.
examples: She made a good argument for a longer recess.
The writer gave three arguments for planting trees.
His argument convinced the class.

easy.def: The part of your body between your shoulder and your hand.
examples: Raise your arm.
My arm is strong.
She hugged me with both arms.

more.def: The long part of the body between the shoulder and the hand.
examples: He raised his arm to ask a question.
An octopus has eight arms.
The baby fell asleep in her mother's arms.

related.def: As much as your arms can hold.

easy.def: Having a weapon.
examples: The knight was armed with a sword.
The guards were armed.
He was armed with a spear.

more.def: Carrying a weapon, or equipped with something to protect or fight.
examples: The knight was armed with a sword and a shield.
The armed guards stood at the castle gate.
The explorers were armed with maps and lanterns.

easy.def: Metal clothes that protect a fighter.
examples: The knight wore armor.
The armor is shiny.
Armor is heavy.

more.def: A strong covering that protects the body, such as the metal suits that knights wore.
examples: The knight put on his heavy armor.
The armor was shiny and cold.
A turtle's shell is like armor.

easy.def: A large group of soldiers.
examples: The army marched through the town.
An army guards the country.
Soldiers in the army wear uniforms.

more.def: A large, organized group of soldiers who fight on land.
examples: The army marched across the mountains.
A country's army protects its borders.
He joined the army after school.

easy.def: On all sides of something, or in a circle.
examples: We sat around the fire.
The dog ran around the tree.
A fence is around the yard.

more.def: On every side of something, in a circle, or in different parts of a place.
examples: The planets travel around the sun.
We walked around the lake before lunch.
She looked around the room for her lost sock.

easy.def: Close by.
examples: Is anyone around?
Look around.
There are many birds around.

more.def: In the area nearby, or about a certain amount.
examples: There are not many people around early in the morning.
The class turned around when the door opened.
The game will begin at around noon.

easy.def: To put things in order.
examples: Arrange the books.
She arranged the flowers.
He arranges the chairs.

more.def: To put things in a certain order or position.
examples: Arrange the books by size.
She arranged the flowers in a vase.
He arranged the chairs in a circle.

easy.def: To plan.
examples: We arranged a picnic.
Mom arranged a ride.
He arranges the trip.

more.def: To plan or set up something ahead of time.
examples: Mom arranged a ride for us.
We arranged a picnic for Saturday.
The teacher arranged a field trip.

easy.def: The way things are put in order.
examples: The arrangement of the desks is new.
The flowers are in a nice arrangement.
The seating arrangement changed.

more.def: The way in which things are placed or put in order.
examples: The arrangement of the desks changed each month.
She made a pretty arrangement of flowers.
The seating arrangement put friends together.

easy.def: To catch a person who did something against the law.
examples: The police arrested the thief.
An officer arrested the man.
They arrest people who break the law.

more.def: To catch someone and hold them because they are thought to have broken the law.
examples: The police arrested the man who stole the bike.
Officers arrest people who break the law.
The sheriff arrested the thief at the train station.

easy.def: Coming to a place.
examples: The arrival of the bus was late.
We waited for her arrival.
The arrival of spring is soon.

more.def: The act of reaching a place.
examples: The arrival of the train was five minutes late.
We waited for the arrival of our guests.
The arrival of spring brings flowers.

easy.def: To get to a place.
examples: We arrive at noon.
The bus arrived.
She arrived at school.

more.def: To reach a place after traveling.
examples: We arrived at the campsite just before dark.
The train arrives at four o'clock.
Grandma arrived with a big bag of presents.

easy.def: A sign that points the way.
examples: Follow the arrow.
The arrow points left.
The arrow shows the exit.

more.def: A sign shaped like a line with a point at the end, used to show a direction.
examples: Follow the arrow on the sign.
The arrow points to the exit.
A red arrow showed us which way to turn.

easy.def: A thin stick shot from a bow.
examples: The arrow hit the target.
The archer shot an arrow.
He held an arrow.

more.def: A thin, straight stick with a point, shot from a bow.
examples: The archer shot an arrow at the target.
The arrow flew through the air.
He pulled an arrow from his quiver.

easy.def: Drawing, painting and other things you make.
examples: I love art class.
Art is fun.
Her art is on the wall.

more.def: Pictures, sculptures and other things that people make to show ideas or feelings.
examples: The art in the museum is hundreds of years old.
We painted flowers in art class.
She loves music, dance and art.

easy.def: A piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine.
examples: I read an article about space.
The article had a picture.
She wrote an article.

more.def: A piece of writing in a newspaper, magazine or website about a certain subject.
examples: The newspaper ran an article about the new park.
Our class read an article about whales.
He wrote an article for the school paper.

easy.def: A thing.
examples: A hat is an article of clothing.
He lost an article.
This is a useful article.

more.def: One single thing, especially one of a group of things.
examples: A coat is an article of clothing.
The lost article was returned to its owner.
Each article in the box was wrapped in paper.

easy.def: A person who makes art.
examples: The artist paints pictures.
My mom is an artist.
The artist used bright colors.

more.def: A person who creates art, such as paintings or music.
examples: The artist painted a picture of the sea.
A street artist drew pictures with chalk.
My aunt is an artist who makes clay pots.

easy.def: Painting, music, dance and other creative subjects.
examples: I like the arts.
We study the arts at school.
The arts are fun.

more.def: Creative subjects and activities such as painting, music, dancing and drama.
examples: I take part in the arts after school.
The school has a strong program in the arts.
Music and drama are part of the arts.
